plan.name: ADVentura

plan.name: ADVentura Blue Eyed Jack's Revenge
plan.wrapper: Mexican San Andres Colorado (base blend); Mexican San Andres Maduro (High Tide variant)
plan.filler: Dominican - one source (Cigar Coop) has an internal inconsistency, its own blend-summary box says 'Dominican filler' while its body text says 'aged Nicaraguan fillers'; 3 other sources (Cigar Inspector, The Cigar Authority, Neptune Cigar) say Dominican filler only. plan.background: One line with a base blend plus a Maduro wrapper variant sub-named 'High Tide' - confirmed by Cigar Coop as 'adding a Maduro offering to the Blue Eyed Jack's Revenge line' (same binder/filler, different wrapper), not two separate lines. plan.name: Asylum
plan.story_short: Asylum was created in 2012 by Tom Lazuka, a former Camacho and Davidoff sales rep, together with Christian Eiroa, and is sold as its own brand rather than under the CLE name. Lazuka's pitch was oversized cigars of 60 to 80 ring gauge, which Eiroa reportedly dismissed as a bad idea before agreeing to make them at his factory in Danlí, Honduras. Its blends favor value and bold, full-flavored profiles in very large ring gauges.

plan.name: Asylum 13 Cool Brew
plan.background: A coffee/cold-brew flavor-infused variant of Asylum 13.

plan.name: Asylum 13 "Split Personality"
plan.background: Released June 2025. Despite the 'split personality' name/premise implying two blends, halfwheel's review found it is actually ONE blend - a Honduran puro flavored to taste like a banana split (banana, butterscotch, vanilla notes).

plan.name: Asylum 13 "The Ogre"
plan.background: A gigante-format Asylum 13 release with a barber-pole wrapper (alternating Candela and Habano leaves).

plan.name: Asylum 13
plan.background: Created in 2012 by Tom Lazuka (a former Camacho/Davidoff sales rep), in partnership with Christian Eiroa shortly after Eiroa's Davidoff non-compete expired. Lazuka pitched oversized 60-80 ring gauge cigars after seeing retailers sell out of them; Eiroa reportedly called the idea 'the worst idea he had ever heard' and named the brand Asylum as a joke at Lazuka's expense, but agreed to produce it anyway. Asylum is sold as its own standalone brand (not badged 'CLE'), but is made at Christian Eiroa's own factory - The CLE Factory (a converted 1975 movie theater) in Danli, Honduras. Blend philosophy is practical/value-driven rather than 'masterpiece' blending - Lazuka has said they started by asking what tobacco they had enough of to make a million cigars - reflected in very large ring gauges (50-80) and bold, spicy, full-flavored profiles at aggressive price points.

plan.name: Asylum "Serenity Now, Insanity Later"
plan.wrapper: Two variants: Connecticut (Serenity Now) / Mexican San Andres Habano (Insanity Later)
plan.binder: Honduran (Serenity Now, partial); not fully disclosed (Insanity Later)
plan.filler: Partially undisclosed - includes an unspecified South American component (Serenity Now); not fully disclosed (Insanity Later)
plan.background: Released March/April 2024. Two distinct blends packaged together in one 100-count box, 50 of each: 'Serenity Now' (mild/smooth, Connecticut wrapper over Honduran binder plus an undisclosed South American filler component) and 'Insanity Later' (bold/aggressive, Mexican San Andres habano wrapper). Binder/filler for both blends are only partially disclosed by the manufacturer - not fabricating the missing pieces.

plan.name: CLE Connecticut
plan.background: This is a real, distinct, currently active core line. CLE Cigar Company was founded July 2012 by Christian Eiroa (son of Julio Eiroa, founder of the Eiroa tobacco dynasty and later Camacho Cigars), after Christian left Camacho in 2011. The factory occupies a converted 1975 movie theater ('Cine Aladino') in Danli, Honduras that once belonged to his grandfather, Antonio Kafati.

plan.background: Confirmed a distinct line, NOT another name for the already-listed Camacho Triple Maduro (which uses a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper) - Camacho Broadleaf instead uses Honduran-grown broadleaf, a different wrapper origin. Announced July 2023, released September 2023. Spotlights Honduran-grown broadleaf tobacco; positioned as a bold, full-bodied offering.

This is Davidoff/Camacho's annual limited-edition release, the successor to Camacho's long-running 'Liberty Series' (2002-2024) - billed as 'a Camacho limited edition without a fancy name,' focused on tobacco blending over a thematic concept.

plan.name: E.P. Carrillo 5 Year Anniversary
plan.background: Released August 15, 2014 to commemorate the fifth anniversary of E.P. Carrillo, the company Ernesto Perez-Carrillo founded in 2009 after leaving General Cigar. A limited, one-time fall release produced in only 3,000 ten-count boxes, made at Tabacalera La Alianza in the Dominican Republic.

plan.name: E.P. Carrillo Battleborn
plan.background: Marketed as 'Perez-Carrillo Battleborn,' this limited-edition line honors Lionel H. McKoy, a U.S. Navy Gulf War veteran who joined Casa Carrillo as shipping manager in 2017. Ernesto Perez-Carrillo III created the line after McKoy shared his military story with him; proceeds support veteran and first-responder charities including the Fisher House Foundation.

plan.name: E.P. Carrillo Cardinal Impact Maduro
plan.background: Cardinal Impact is the 2016 relaunch of E.P. Carrillo's original 2012 Cardinal line, rebuilt with modified blends and box-pressed construction.

plan.name: E.P. Carrillo Encore Black
plan.background: One of three 2024 line extensions that elevated Encore from a sub-line of the Perez-Carrillo portfolio into its own standalone brand. Swaps the original Encore's all-Nicaraguan, medium-bodied blend for a dark Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper over San Andres binder, produced at Casa Carrillo (formerly Tabacalera La Alianza).

plan.name: E.P. Carrillo Encore El Futuro
plan.background: The first regular-production line extension of Encore since its 2018 launch, unveiled April 2022. Unlike the original Encore's Ecuadorian wrapper, El Futuro uses an all-Nicaraguan wrapper/binder/filler blend, tobaccos aged in tercios before rolling. Production at Tabacalera La Alianza S.A., initial limited run of 1,000 boxes ahead of the 2022 PCA trade show.

plan.name: E.P. Carrillo Encore TAA Exclusive (Encore TAA 656)
plan.background: Released 2020 exclusively for Tobacconists Association of America (TAA) retailers, the Encore TAA 656 is an all-Nicaraguan-tobacco expression of Encore, a departure from the standard Encore's Ecuadorian-wrapper blend. Its extreme box press gives the 6x56 'Toro Gordo' vitola an oval-like cross-section. Announced March 2020, shipped August 2020, limited to 750 boxes of 10, produced at Tabacalera La Alianza S.A.

plan.name: E.P. Carrillo INCH Colorado

plan.name: E.P. Carrillo INCH Limited Edition 2019

plan.name: E.P. Carrillo Interlude Maduro
plan.background: Interlude debuted at the 2016 IPCPR trade show as part of E.P. Carrillo's 'Dimension Series,' created to fill a portfolio gap for short, thinner, quick smokes. plan.name: E.P. Carrillo Interlude Natural

plan.name: Davidoff Year of the Horse Limited Edition 2026
plan.filler: Proprietary hybrid tobaccos with three vintage fillers, aged over four decades (per brand description)
plan.background: Newest entry in Davidoff's long-running Lunar New Year/zodiac limited edition series (releases since 2013).
vitolas: Year of the Horse Flagship Exclusive 6x52 torpedo

plan.name: Deadwood Dominicana Buenas Noches
plan.background: 'Dominicana' is a distinct sub-line departing from Deadwood's usual Nicaraguan-tobacco blends toward Dominican-puro-oriented tobacco. Revealed as the mystery cigar at a 2025 'Freestyle Live' event.

plan.name: Deadwood Fat Bottom Betty
plan.background: One of the 4 core Deadwood 'Wild Bunch' blends, debuted 2013 per founder Vaughn Boyd. The Gordito size is a size extension (added October 2019), not a separate blend.

plan.name: Deadwood Sweet Jane Dia de los Muertos Limited Edition 2024
plan.background: A limited-edition variant of the Sweet Jane blend (one of Deadwood's 4 core 'Wild Bunch' blends). Originally a Drew Estate Lounge exclusive (2019), returned nationally as a limited edition in 2024, and again in 2025.

plan.name: Domain Cigars
plan.story_short: Domain is an independent brand founded in March 2024 by Daniel Lance, who has a cigar-retail background, and Esteban Disla, a cigar maker with roughly ten years at Fabrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño and blends for CAO, Toraño and Alec Bradley. It operates as a full-service tobacco company covering agriculture, processing, brokering and cigar making in Estelí, Nicaragua.

plan.name: Domain Entropy
plan.background: Domain's third regular-production line (after Neutron and Negentropy, both debuted April 2024). A refined, regular-production evolution of an earlier limited prototype called 'No7B' - roughly 90% of Entropy's blend is derived from Negentropy, with a different broadleaf crop and one filler viso change versus the No7B prototype. Pre-orders opened October 2024; began shipping to retailers around November 2024.

plan.name: Don Diego
plan.story_short: Don Diego is currently distributed in the U.S. by Altadis USA. Retailers categorize it as Dominican-made; that origin and the brand's history have not been confirmed from a primary source.

plan.name: Don Diego
plan.background: Core/original line.

plan.name: Dos Amigos
plan.story_short: Dos Amigos (1987) is a 2025 brand conceived in Barcelona by Jordi Llorens and Isidre Pineda, with its cigars produced in Nicaragua. It launched internationally at InterTabac 2025 and has been covered mainly by European trade press.

plan.name: Dos Amigos 1987
plan.background: Launched deliberately as a focused two-vitola portfolio (not a 3-vitola lineup). Each vitola also carries its own marketing nickname: the Robusto is called 'Paster' and the Toro is called 'Sidecar.' Tobacco aged a minimum of 2 years; profile described as mild, with sweetness and a touch of spice.

plan.name: Sobremesa Brûlée
plan.background: Sobremesa Brûlée from Dunbarton Tobacco & Trust: Ecuador Connecticut Shade (Sumatra-seed 'G2BW') wrapper, Mexican San Andres Negro binder, Nicaraguan filler.

plan.name: Gispert
plan.story_short: Gispert is distributed by Altadis USA, which launched the Gispert Intenso line extension in 2017 as a collaboration with A.J. Fernandez. Retailers categorize it as Dominican-made; its founding history has not been confirmed.

plan.name: Gispert
plan.background: Distributed by Altadis USA, confirmed via trade-press coverage of the 2017 'Gispert Intenso' line extension launch (a collaboration with A.J. Fernandez).

plan.name: H. Upmann 1844 Añejo
plan.wrapper: Ecuadorian Habano (described as dark, oily, double-fermented)
plan.background: All tobaccos aged a minimum of 5 years ('anejo' = aged/old). Medium-to-full-bodied; notes of earth, cocoa, cinnamon, leather, dark fruit/citrus.

plan.name: H. Upmann 1844 Classic
plan.background: Released 2021 by Altadis USA as part of the '1844' portfolio (named for H. Upmann's 1844 founding year), positioned as a tribute to the brand's Cuban heritage. Medium-bodied; notes of leather, nutmeg, spice, coffee, toast, sweet cream.

plan.name: H. Upmann by AJ Fernandez
plan.binder: Corojo '99 (Nicaraguan) - one retailer (JR Cigars) instead lists 'Vintage San Andres,' possibly reflecting a blend refresh since 2017; not resolved
plan.background: Launched by Altadis USA in 2017, a collaboration with A.J. Fernandez marking a departure from Upmann's traditional Dominican/mild profile toward a medium-to-full-bodied blend.

plan.name: H. Upmann Nicaragua AJ Fernandez Heritage
plan.background: Debuted January 2022 at TPE (Tobacco Plus Expo). Ecuadorian), positioned as a heritage/legacy-style release. Medium to medium-full strength; notes of earthiness, spice, sweetness.

plan.name: H. Upmann Vintage Cameroon
plan.background: Marketed as a revival of H. Upmann's pre-1995 character, before a Cameroon wrapper shortage forced a recipe change. Medium strength.

vitolas: Half Corona 'Fresh Out the Oven' Broadleaf 3.5x44 corona

plan.name: HVC La Decoración
plan.wrapper: Ecuadorian (also referred to as 'Ecuadorian 2000' in some sourcing)
plan.background: The real product is 'La Decoración' ('Reinier Lorenzo's Ode to Cuban Artistry'), a new regular-production line shown at PCA 2026, shipping to stores from ~April 7, 2026.

plan.name: Henry Clay
plan.story_short: Henry Clay was founded in the 1840s in Cuba by Spanish immigrant Julian Alvarez Granda and named for the American statesman. After the Cuban original was nationalized, the U.S. trademark passed through Henry Clay & Bock Co. to Consolidated Cigar Corporation, which began making non-Cuban Henry Clays by 1986 and was later acquired by Altadis. Today's lines are made in several countries: the core line in the Dominican Republic, War Hawk in Honduras and War Hawk Rebellious in Nicaragua.

plan.name: Henry Clay Rustic Cheroot
plan.background: Blend name 'Capa Dura,' described by Altadis as producing 'a rich, stronger blend.' Includes 'reborn' (recycled/repurposed) leaf in the filler. Announced March 1, 2018; national rollout April 2018. At launch: 20-count boxes, $4.25/cigar.

plan.name: Henry Clay War Hawk Rebellious
plan.background: CLARIFICATION: confirmed to be a distinct limited-edition blend, NOT simply a size/vitola within the regular War Hawk line - different wrapper, different origin, different factory, different blender. A Nicaraguan puro, single-vitola limited edition. Released July 2020; limited run of 1,200 boxes of 20 (24,000 cigars total). Launch price $9.60/cigar, $192/box of 20.

plan.name: Henry Clay War Hawk
plan.background: Launched March 2019, the first Henry Clay product with an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper.

plan.name: Henry Clay
plan.wrapper: Connecticut Broadleaf (maduro) - confirmed on specific vitolas; some sources instead describe Ecuadorian Sumatra/Connecticut Shade, unresolved conflict
plan.filler: Dominican (some sources add Honduran/Nicaraguan/Peruvian as brand-wide filler components, not confirmed which specific SKUs these apply to)
plan.background: Core/general-market line. Handmade, medium-to-full-bodied.

plan.name: Illusione Epernay Tuonela
plan.background: A San Andres-wrapper variant of Epernay released May 2025 (regular production, not limited).

plan.name: Brick House Double Connecticut
plan.background: Ecuador Habano-seed) and profile (mellow to medium vs. the core line's fuller body).

plan.name: Brick House
plan.background: Founded on a story from J.C. Newman founder Julius Caesar Newman, who named the brand after a communal Hungarian gathering house. Discontinued during the Depression, revived by descendants Bobby and Eric Newman using Cuban-seed tobacco grown in Nicaragua. Made at J.C. Newman's PENSA factory in Esteli, Nicaragua - a value-priced line, unrelated to the separately-owned HVC brand despite a superficial naming resemblance some might assume.

plan.name: Diamond Crown
plan.background: Diamond Crown from J.C. Newman: Connecticut Shade (double-fermented, long-aged) wrapper, Dominican binder, Multi-country filler.

plan.name: El Baton
plan.background: Originally created by founder Julius Caesar 'J.C.' Newman in 1914 as a nickel cigar hand-rolled in Cleveland, Ohio using Cuban tobacco; disappeared from the market in the 1920s as machine-made cigars took over. Revived in 2008 by 4th-generation Eric and Bobby Newman as the company's first all-Nicaraguan puro, then relaunched again in 2022/2024 with a bolder blend, higher-grade wrapper, and redesigned bands/boxes. Earned a 91 rating from Cigar Aficionado and was Cigar Journal's #2 Cigar of the Year (2023).

plan.name: JFR 20th Anniversary
plan.background: A regular-production line celebrating 20 years of the JFR brand (2005-2025), released by Aganorsa Leaf in 2025.

plan.name: Joya de Nicaragua Cinco Décadas Fundador
plan.background: The Fundador name honors Juan Francisco Bermejo and Simón Camacho, credited with advancing Nicaragua's cigar industry.

plan.name: Joya de Nicaragua Clásico Medio Siglo
plan.wrapper: Connecticut-Ecuador (Nicaraguan H. Criollo per JDN official site)
plan.background: Clásico Medio Siglo ("half century") is JDN's modern evolution of its original, most popular cigar, first rolled in Nicaragua over fifty years ago. It was added for international markets circa 2019-2020 and later brought to the U.S. It delivers an intensified Nicaraguan flavor profile of woody, leathery, cocoa and earthy-sweet notes versus the original Clásico.

plan.name: Joya de Nicaragua Cuatro Cinco Edición Europa
plan.filler: Nicaraguan, including 5-year-old ligero aged in spent rum barrels
plan.background: Cuatro Cinco Edición Europa is a European-market-exclusive regional variant of JDN's Cuatro Cinco line, announced September 2022 at Intertabac in Germany - the third regional exclusive in the Cuatro Cinco family, following an Asian exclusive (2020) and an American edition (2021). The original Cuatro Cinco debuted in 2013 as an all-Nicaraguan puro limited edition celebrating JDN's 45th anniversary; the blend was later modified (Dominican binder added) into the ongoing 'Reserva Especial,' and Edición Europa builds on that modified recipe with rum-barrel-aged ligero filler.

plan.name: Joya de Nicaragua Cuatro Cinco Pata Negra
plan.background: Cuatro Cinco Pata Negra is the most recent installment (announced for Spain in 2026) of JDN's annual Spain-exclusive Pata Negra prestige series, which each year reimagines one of JDN's core blends in an elevated, extra-aged expression limited to that market. This edition applies the Pata Negra treatment to the Cuatro Cinco (Reserva Especial) blend, originally created in 2013 as a 45th-anniversary limited edition featuring white-oak-barrel-aged tobacco.

plan.name: Joya de Nicaragua Cuatro Cinco Secret Cask
plan.filler: 100% Nicaraguan, including five-year-aged ligero matured in charred white-oak casks that previously held spirits
plan.background: Cuatro Cinco Secret Cask pays homage to the original 2013 Cuatro Cinco Edición Limitada, JDN's 45th-anniversary release and the first cigar in its Obras Maestras ultra-premium collection, which sold out its 4,500-box run. Secret Cask uses the identical all-Nicaraguan puro blend but with tobacco aged in charred oak spirit casks set aside in 2013. Released November 2025 in a limited run of 1,500 boxes of 10 (700 allocated to the U.S.), each box includes a small 'mini-casket' of filler tobacco replicating the aging process.

plan.name: CyB by Joya de Nicaragua
plan.background: CyB (originally launched as "Cuenca y Blanco") was the first collaboration between Joya de Nicaragua and cigar maker Jose Blanco following his 2011 arrival at the company, after roughly a year of development. It marked a departure from JDN's tradition of all-Nicaraguan puros, blending tobaccos from four countries: Nicaragua, Dominican Republic, Ecuador and Peru. A Lancero Fino vitola (7 x 38) was later released in 2013 as a TAA exclusive.

plan.name: Flor de Nicaragua Ventus Aurum
plan.filler: Nicaraguan (Habano seed, grown in Estelí and Jalapa)
plan.background: Ventus Aurum is a tier within Joya de Nicaragua's Flor de Nicaragua brand, one of JDN's oldest lines, historically sold mainly in northern Europe/Spain rather than the U.S. market. It uses tobaccos grown in the selected valleys of Estelí and Jalapa in northern Nicaragua.

plan.name: Joya de Nicaragua Rosalones Reserva
plan.background: Rosalones Reserva is the fuller-bodied, all-Nicaraguan-leaf counterpart within the Rosalones family, wrapped in Nicaraguan Habano Criollo Colorado versus the Connecticut-seed wrapper of standard Rosalones (CT). It made its first official U.S. market debut alongside Rosalones CT in 2026, sold as a genuinely separate blend rather than a packaging variant. An earlier/international 'Rosalones Reserva' (vitola codes R546, R650, RR444) has also circulated via European retailers with a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper, consistent in character with the 2026 U.S. version.
vitolas: R546 (Corona Gorda, legacy/international sizing) 5.5x46 corona gorda

plan.name: Joya de Nicaragua Rosalones (CT)
plan.background: Rosalones is one of Joya de Nicaragua's original, longest-running brands, historically sold mainly in European markets. In 2026 JDN brought Rosalones to the U.S. market for the first time as "Rosalones CT," a Connecticut-seed-wrapped, milder entry in the Rosalones family, alongside the darker Rosalones Reserva. Older international packagings of the base Rosalones/Rosalones Auténticos line (predating the 2026 U.S. launch) used a Habano-seed Colorado Maduro wrapper and different vitola naming (e.g., "552," "448 Consul"), suggesting the blend/wrapper has varied by market and over time.

plan.name: Kristoff Guardrail
plan.background: The real product is 'Kristoff Guardrail,' debuted 2022, ranked #8 on Cigar Coop's 2023 Cigar of the Year countdown.

plan.name: Kristoff Nicaragua
plan.background: Kristoff Nicaragua from Kristoff: Nicaraguan Habano wrapper, Nicaraguan Corojo binder, Nicaraguan (Condega, Esteli, Jalapa) filler.

plan.name: Kristoff PCA 2024 Signature Series
plan.background: Kristoff PCA 2024 Signature Series from Kristoff: Mexican San Andres wrapper, Indonesian binder, Nicaraguan filler.

plan.name: Kristoff TAA Exclusive 2023
plan.background: 'Taa' = TAA (Tobacconists' Association of America), an annual exclusive-retailer release; '23' = 2023.

plan.name: Kristoff Tres Compadres
plan.background: 'Tres' = Tres Compadres ('three friends/compadres,' honoring Glen Case's friends Rolando Villamil and Chuck Finch). Introduced at 2023 PCA alongside Kristoff Nicaragua.

plan.name: La Flor Dominicana Capitulo II (Chapter Two)
plan.background: Follow-up to the limited 'Chapter One' (first blend by Antonio Gomez, son of Litto Gomez; Chapter One was capped at 100,000 cigars / 10,000 boxes). Unveiled at the 2014 IPCPR Trade Show.

plan.name: La Flor Dominicana La Nox
plan.filler: Dominican Piloto Cubano and Dominican Pelo de Oro (La Canela farm)
plan.background: Unveiled at the 2015 IPCPR Trade Show.

plan.name: La Flor Dominicana La Volcada
plan.background: Shown at the 2017 IPCPR Trade Show, retail availability late 2017/early 2018. Explicitly described by the brand as part of a series of limited production releases.

plan.name: La Flor Dominicana Ligero
plan.background: Offered in Natural and Oscuro (darkest Ecuadorian Sumatra) wrapper styles, sometimes called 'Ligero Oscuro.'

plan.name: La Flor Dominicana Oro
plan.background: Originally launched at the 2012 IPCPR Trade Show with 3 sizes (one Chisel + two parejo, all 6x54), in gold tubos, 5-count boxes. Expanded with 3 new sizes in October 2025 (current, actively expanding regular-production line, not limited edition). Offered in Natural and Maduro sub-lines.

vitolas: Small Batch Short Perfecto 4.5x62 short perfecto

plan.name: Lampert 1593 (Edición Blanca)
plan.background: The Lampert 1593 line commemorates the year the Lampert family received its first heraldic crest, tying the brand's premium cigars to the family's claimed European noble heritage. Unlike Lampert's Nicaraguan-made 1675 series, 1593 is produced by Edgar Julian Sued at Julian Sued & Compania in Tamboril, Dominican Republic. It was soft-launched exclusively through Small Batch Cigar (Orange, CA) in June 2022 as the Edición Blanca, with a national U.S. rollout in 2023, and a Short Robusto format made available in Switzerland and Sweden.

plan.name: Lampert 1675 Edición Morado
plan.background: Edición Morado is a later entry in Lampert's 1675 series, produced for aficionados wanting a deeper, darker profile than the Azúl while retaining the brand's signature smoothness. Rolled at Fábrica AGROTABACOS in Nicaragua using tobacco aged 3-5 years.

plan.name: Lampert 1675 Edición Verde
plan.background: Edición Verde is the fifth blend released in Lampert's 1675 Edición Series, debuting at InterTabac 2025. Manufactured at AgroIndustrial Nicaraguense de Tabacos S.A.; each vitola is oval-pressed and uses tobacco aged five years, positioned as Lampert's fullest-bodied 1675 release to date. Only the Toro Grande ships to the U.S.; Robusto Grande and Short Robusto are Europe-only.

plan.name: Lampert Baba Yaga
plan.background: Baba Yaga is a limited-edition Lampert Cigars release manufactured at Tabacos de Costa Rica, marking a departure from the brand's usual Nicaraguan (1675) and Dominican (1593) production. Named after the mythical witch of Slavic folklore, the line was deliberately shrouded in mystery at launch, with founder Dr. Stefan Lampert withholding binder and filler details, saying the blend was 'created to offer something different - something that captures mystery, strength, and craftsmanship in one cigar.' Announced/released in June 2026 in a single Toro vitola.

plan.name: Lampert Family Reserve
plan.background: Lampert Family Reserve is an annually-dated limited release produced in partnership with Hendrik Kelner Jr. at the Kelner Boutique Factory (KBF) in Santiago de los Caballeros, Dominican Republic. First shipped as 'Family Reserve 2021' in July 2022, packaged in okoume-wood boxes (the same wood used by Davidoff). A 'Family Reserve 2023' edition followed in December 2023 with new banding but the same underlying blend.

plan.name: Lampert Lawyer
plan.background: Lampert deliberately withholds the wrapper, binder, and filler origins for this blend, positioning it around 'balance, discretion, and quiet confidence.' Founder Dr.

plan.name: Lampert Limitada
plan.background: Limitada is Lampert Cigars' annual limited-edition retailer-exclusive series, launched in 2022 as part of the 'Golden Retailer Program' with a Salomones vitola. Founder Dr. Stefan Lampert releases a new Limitada blend most years for the brand's top retail accounts, each edition typically using a different wrapper/binder/filler combination and vitola.

plan.name: Las Cabrillas
plan.story_short: Las Cabrillas is a long-running line named for New World explorers such as Balboa, De Soto, Cortez and Columbus. It is rolled in Honduras with all-Mexican San Andrés binder and filler, an unusual combination, and comes in Connecticut Shade natural and San Andrés maduro wrappers.

plan.name: Montecristo 1935 Anniversary
plan.background: A family of releases, not one blend - includes 'Edicion Diamante' and a newer 'Edicion Doble Diamante' sub-release (a separate blend/price tier, not a vitola name).

plan.name: Montecristo Espada
plan.background: Three distinct sub-lines under the Espada name, each a genuinely different blend, not just vitola variants of one product.

plan.name: Montecristo M
plan.background: Made by A.J. Fernandez in Esteli, Nicaragua.

plan.name: Montecristo Nicaragua Series
plan.background: 100% Nicaraguan, made by A.J. Fernandez in Esteli.

plan.name: Montecristo Platinum Series
plan.background: Montecristo Platinum Series from Montecristo: San Andres Cubano (Mexico) wrapper, Dominican binder, Dominican, Nicaraguan, Peruvian filler.

plan.name: Don Pepin Garcia E.R.H.
plan.background: "El Rey de los Habanos" - a reformulated 2025 revival of a 2014-era Don Pepin Garcia release, released by My Father Cigars as part of the Don Pepin Garcia family. Described by the maker as a signature peppery blend.

plan.name: Flor de las Antillas Maduro
plan.background: Maduro-wrapped expression of My Father's Flor de las Antillas line. Debuted April 2015 as a Federal Cigar retailer exclusive, then expanded to regular production by the November 2016 IPCPR trade show.

plan.name: Fonseca Mexico Edition
plan.background: Mexican San Andres-wrapped expression of Fonseca by My Father, debuted mid-2020 with the Robusto vitola formalized into the regular lineup by March 2024.

plan.name: La Duena
plan.background: Originally released around 2011, named as a tribute to Janny Garcia, blended by Jaime Garcia in collaboration with Pete Johnson of Tatuaje.

plan.name: My Father La Gran Oferta
plan.background: Value/everyday-smoke line launched at the 2018 IPCPR trade show, sold in boxes of 20.

plan.name: Oliva Serie G Maduro
plan.wrapper: Connecticut Broadleaf (per halfwheel and Cigar Aficionado spec data)
plan.background: Some retailer/manufacturer marketing copy (olivacigar.com, cigarsinternational.com) describes the wrapper as Mexican or a blended 'Connecticut Broadleaf Mexican San Andres' descriptor - treated as loose marketing language rather than a factual contradiction; Connecticut Broadleaf is used here per the more rigorous halfwheel/Cigar Aficionado spec sheets.

plan.name: Omar Ortez
plan.story_short: Omar Ortez is distributed by Altadis USA and remains active, with a new three-count fresh pack announced in 2025. Retailers and the Altadis product listing point to Honduran manufacture, though its founding year and history are unconfirmed.

plan.name: Omar Ortez Maduro
plan.background: Official Altadis product URL is 'omar-ortez-honduran-maduro,' supporting a Honduran origin for this specific line.

plan.name: Omar Ortez Originals
plan.background: Distributed by Altadis USA (confirmed via official altadisusa.com/cigars/omar-ortez/ URL structure and a July 2025 Cigar Coop article about a new 'Omar Ortez 3-Count Fresh Pack' at that year's Altadis Traveling Road Show, confirming the brand is still active).

plan.name: Onyx
plan.story_short: Onyx was founded in 2000 and named for its original near-black Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. Now distributed and manufactured by Altadis USA, it has grown from a single Dominican maduro line into three lines spanning Dominican and Nicaraguan-puro blends.

plan.name: Onyx Bold Nicaragua
plan.background: Released 2020. A Nicaraguan-puro-adjacent expression with a dark San Andres wrapper, positioned as the brand's more intense/bold departure from the original Dominican maduro.

plan.name: Onyx Reserve
plan.background: The original/legacy blend. Rich, medium-to-full-bodied maduro; several vitolas are square-pressed.

plan.name: Onyx Vintage Nicaragua
plan.background: Released September 2023 - a 100% Nicaraguan-puro release built around an extra-aged Habano Nicaragua wrapper from a 2019 harvest. Positioned as medium-to-full-bodied, deliberately less intense than Onyx Bold Nicaragua and with a lighter wrapper color, distinguishing it from the brand's traditional dark 'black/onyx' look while still carrying the Onyx name. Flavor notes: black pepper, leather, earth, dark chocolate, sweetness.

plan.name: Ozgener Karatoba
plan.background: Ozgener Karatoba from Ozgener: Ecuador-grown Sumatra-seed wrapper, Nicaragua binder, Dominican Republic and Nicaragua filler.

plan.name: Perdomo Two Guys Smoke Shop 40th Anniversary
plan.background: A retailer-exclusive limited edition released August 4, 2025 to commemorate the retailer Two Guys Smoke Shop's 40th anniversary - NOT a Perdomo-company anniversary release. Limited to 400 ten-count boxes.

plan.name: Perdomo Habano Bourbon Barrel-Aged Connecticut
plan.background: Ecuadoran Connecticut wrapper aged 6+ years then bourbon-barrel finished 6 additional months.

plan.name: Perdomo Legacy
plan.wrapper: Connecticut, Maduro, or Nicaraguan Shade Grown (3 editions, see vitolas)
plan.background: Launched at the 2025 PCA trade show.

plan.name: Perdomo Reserve 10th Anniversary Maduro
plan.background: Perdomo Reserve 10th Anniversary Maduro from Perdomo: Nicaraguan Maduro (bourbon-barrel-aged) wrapper, Nicaraguan binder, Nicaraguan filler.

plan.name: Perdomo Reserve 10th Anniversary Sun Grown
plan.background: Perdomo Reserve 10th Anniversary Sun Grown from Perdomo: Nicaraguan Sun Grown (bourbon-barrel-aged) wrapper, Nicaraguan binder, Nicaraguan filler.

plan.name: Primo del Rey
plan.story_short: Primo del Rey cigars are handmade in Honduras according to current retailer listings. No founder, founding date or parent company has been found, and only a small number of retailers currently carry it.

plan.name: Primo del Rey
plan.background: Mild-to-medium / medium-bodied, marketed as affordable and aromatic; flavor notes cited by retailers include leather, cedar, coffee, cream, and vanilla.

plan.name: RoMa Craft Intemperance EC XVIII
plan.background: Part of RoMa Craft's Prohibition-era-themed Intemperance concept (launched 2012); 'EC' = Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper, 'XVIII' references the 18th Amendment (which enacted Prohibition).

plan.name: RoMa Craft Intemperance Whiskey Rebellion 1794
plan.background: A third Intemperance sub-blend, named for the actual 1794 U.S. Whiskey Rebellion rather than a constitutional amendment (unlike BA XXI and EC XVIII). Vitolas are named for historical American figures of the era.

plan.name: 30th Anniversary
plan.background: Released in 2025 to mark Rocky Patel Premium Cigars' 30th year in business (the company traces its roots to Rocky Patel's 1995 partnership with Phil Zanghi/Indian Tabac). Unveiled at the 2025 PCA trade show and rolled at Patel's Tavicusa factory in Esteli, Nicaragua, it is a box-pressed blend built around an aged Mexican San Andres wrapper, and it was also the first release to carry the company's newly redesigned band/box branding.

plan.name: Bold
plan.binder: Mexican San Andres and Connecticut (dual binder)
plan.background: Bold (originally released and marketed as 'Bold by Nish Patel') was the second blend created by Nish Patel, Rocky Patel's younger brother, following the success of his first line, Xen. It debuted in August 2013 and was built to be a full-bodied, complex smoke, pairing a dark Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper with a dual Mexican San Andres/Connecticut binder over Nicaraguan long fillers. It has since been sold under the broader Rocky Patel Premium Cigars banner as simply 'Bold.'

plan.name: Dark Star
plan.filler: Honduran and Nicaraguan, including tobacco grown from Paraguayan seed
plan.background: Dark Star debuted at the 2023 PCA (Premium Cigar Association) Trade Show and began shipping to retailers on November 30, 2023. It is produced at Plasencia's El Paraiso factory in Honduras and is notable for being the first Rocky Patel release to use a leaf grown from Paraguayan tobacco seed, an ingredient the brand had never used before.

plan.name: Emerald
plan.filler: Nicaraguan and Honduran (including leaf from the Jamastran Valley)
plan.background: Emerald is Rocky Patel's first box-pressed line built specifically to stay on the lighter side of medium-bodied, answering customer demand for a milder option from a brand best known for medium-to-full smokes. It was first shown as an upcoming release at the 2024 Traveling Road Show Tour and began shipping to retailers in December 2024, produced at the TAVICUSA factory in Esteli, Nicaragua.

plan.name: Gold Label
plan.binder: Connecticut Broadleaf and Connecticut Shade (dual binder)
plan.background: Gold Label debuted at the 2024 PCA Trade Show as part of Rocky Patel's newer 'precious metals and stones'-themed lineup, positioned as a more affordable, approachable option relative to his premium-tier blends. It pairs an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with a dual Connecticut binder over Nicaraguan long fillers, and is made at Tabacalera Villa Cuba S.A. in Esteli, Nicaragua.

plan.name: Quarter Century
plan.filler: Nicaraguan (Esteli, Jalapa, Jamastran) and Honduran, plus an undisclosed component
plan.background: Quarter Century is confirmed to be Rocky Patel's 25th Anniversary line, released in 2020 (shipping began August 17, 2020) to mark 25 years since Rocky Patel entered the cigar business in 1995 with Indian Tabac Cigar Co.

plan.name: Sapphire
plan.binder: Dual binder: one leaf from Esteli, Nicaragua and one from the Jamastran Valley, Honduras
plan.filler: Nicaraguan (Condega, Esteli and Jalapa), aged 6-7 years
plan.background: Sapphire is the third entry in Rocky Patel's unofficial 'precious metals and gems' series, following Gold Label and Emerald (both 2024). It debuted at the April 2026 PCA Convention & Trade Show in New Orleans before shipping to retailers as a retailer-exclusive release. Rocky Patel describes it as using older tobaccos than Emerald, making it richer and stronger, and it marks the first commercial use of leaf from his three-year-old Honduran farm; nearly all of the blend aside from the wrapper comes from Patel's own farms.

plan.name: Twentieth Anniversary
plan.wrapper: Honduran (sun-grown; offered in natural and Maduro wrapper options)
plan.background: Released in 2015 to commemorate Rocky Patel's 20th year in the cigar industry (founded 1995), this line kept most of its blend recipe a closely guarded 'trade secret,' disclosing only the regional origins of the tobacco.

plan.name: Vintage 1999
plan.background: Vintage 1999 uses Connecticut shade wrapper leaf harvested in 1999 and aged roughly seven years before use, paired with seven-year-aged Nicaraguan and Dominican ligero filler. Rocky Patel markets it as one of the oldest Connecticut shade wrappers on the market, positioned as an approachable, mild-to-medium everyday smoke for both new and experienced smokers.

plan.name: Year of the Dragon
plan.background: Year of the Dragon was Rocky Patel's inaugural entry into a new Chinese Zodiac-themed limited-edition series, released for Chinese New Year 2024 to honor the dragon as a symbol of power, strength, and prosperity. The blend pairs a Mexican San Andres wrapper with dual Honduran/Nicaraguan binders over all-Nicaraguan filler tobacco aged since 2014, produced at Rocky Patel's TAVICUSA factory in Nicaragua. Limited to 6,000 ten-count boxes for the U.S. market with red-and-gold packaging honoring the Chinese New Year aesthetic.

plan.name: Year of the Snake
plan.wrapper: Nicaraguan Habano (U.S. version); Nicaraguan Habano 2000 Oscuro (International version)
plan.background: Launched at the 2025 PCA Trade Show, Year of the Snake is the second release in Rocky Patel's Chinese Zodiac limited-edition series (following 2024's Year of the Dragon), honoring the serpent's symbolism of transformation, elegance, and mystery. Produced at Tabacalera Villa Cuba S.A. (TAVICUSA) in Esteli, Nicaragua, it was released in two blends: a medium-full U.S. version with Nicaraguan Habano wrapper and a medium-bodied International Exclusive with Habano 2000 Oscuro wrapper. Limited to 6,000 ten-count boxes at $35 per cigar, with festive red-and-gold packaging.

plan.name: Romeo y Julieta 150th Anniversary
plan.background: Commemorates the brand's 1875 founding. Launched by Altadis USA, debuted at Procigar February 2025, national launch at the PCA Trade Show April 2025. Named halfwheel's 2025 #2 Cigar of the Year.

plan.name: Romeo y Julieta Reserve
plan.background: Medium-to-full body, a notable departure from RyJ's traditionally milder profile.

plan.name: Romeo y Julieta Vintage
plan.background: A long-running, current (not discontinued) Dominican line, though some vitolas show as out-of-stock/restock at retail.

plan.name: Saint Luis Rey
plan.story_short: This is the non-Cuban Saint Luis Rey distributed by Altadis USA, which takes its name from a Cuban trademark registered in the 1940s and nationalized in 1960. The modern Honduran blend was created in 1996 by Christian Eiroa, later moved to Flor de Copán, and was reformulated as SLR Gen2 in 2013. It is positioned as accessible premium at roughly $6-9 per cigar.

plan.name: Saint Luis Rey Carenas Ultramar
plan.background: Tribute to 16th-century Spanish trade vessels that sailed 'ultramar' (overseas) from Puerto Carenas carrying tobacco.

plan.name: Saint Luis Rey Carenas
plan.background: Named for Puerto de Carenas, the old name for Havana harbor. Medium-bodied, earthy spice and salty notes, oily Nicaraguan wrapper over an aged Honduran core.

plan.name: Saint Luis Rey Original
plan.background: Full-bodied, crafted in Honduras.

plan.name: Saint Luis Rey Reserva Especial
plan.wrapper: Nicaraguan EMS (natural option) or Mexican San Andres/Morron (maduro option)
plan.filler: Honduran, Nicaraguan, and Peruvian (per a JR Cigars brand-history page; not independently re-confirmed on a current Reserva Especial-specific product page)
plan.background: Handcrafted in Santa Rosa de Copan, Honduras; marketed as a 'super premium' tier within the brand, blending Honduran, Nicaraguan, and Peruvian tobaccos with rich coffee/tobacco notes.

plan.name: Saint Luis Rey Serie G Maduro
plan.background: 'G' reportedly stands for 'gigante' (large ring gauges, 54-60). Fuller-bodied maduro line with a hand-selected Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper.

plan.name: Saint Luis Rey Tabacales
plan.background: Billed as 'the first regular-production Dominican Saint Luis Rey' - the first time in the brand's history a premium SLR has been made in the Dominican Republic, rather than Honduras. A tribute to the tobacco harvest ritual in the Dominican Republic's Cibao Valley. Blend created by Rafael Nodal and the Grupo de Maestros team; described as reduced-strength versus the traditional Honduran-made SLR. Released first week of August 2025, previewed at the 2025 Altadis Traveling Road Show.

plan.name: Santa Clara 1830 50th Anniversary Triple Maduro (also marketed as "Medio Siglo Triple Maduro")
plan.wrapper: Triple Maduro (specific wrapper leaf/fermentation not detailed on the chart itself)
plan.background: A limited 50th-anniversary release.

plan.name: Topper Cigar Company
plan.story_short: Topper Cigar Company is an independent fourth-generation family business founded in 1896 in McSherrystown, Pennsylvania, and now run by Chris Topper. Its cigars are made in Danlí, Honduras, and it is unrelated to J.C. Newman.

plan.name: Topper Danli
plan.background: Topper Danli from Topper Cigar Company: Connecticut Broadleaf (maduro) wrapper, Pennsylvania binder, Dominican, Honduran, and American filler.

plan.name: Trinidad
plan.story_short: This is the non-Cuban Trinidad distributed by Altadis USA, separate from the Cuban original that was created in 1969 at El Laguito in Havana as a diplomatic gift. Altadis relaunched the name around 2017 with Trinidad Santiago, driven by Rafael Nodal, and current lines are made in the Dominican Republic and Nicaragua. The 1969 date is the Cuban original's founding year.

plan.name: Trinidad Espiritu Series No. 1
plan.background: Created 2019 by master blender A.J. Fernandez and Rafael Nodal; first entry in a three-part numbered series, each pairing Trinidad's heritage image with a single-country-themed wrapper showcase. Positioned as a modern tribute to 'golden age' (1960s-70s) Trinidad-style cigars. Full-to-medium-full-bodied.

plan.name: Trinidad Espiritu Series No. 2
plan.background: Released 2021, second entry in the Espiritu numbered series, themed around Brazilian tobacco.

plan.name: Trinidad Espiritu Series No. 3
plan.background: Released late 2024, third entry in the Espiritu numbered series, themed around Mexican San Andres tobacco and tied to Dia de los Muertos.

plan.name: Trinidad Santiago
plan.background: Dominican puro released September 2017, positioned by Altadis USA/Rafael Nodal as the start of a 'resurrection' of the Trinidad brand and the first regular-production Trinidad release since the 2012 limited 'Trinidad Paradox.'

plan.name: Trinidad x Tommy Bahama Island Collection
plan.wrapper: All-Nicaraguan (specific wrapper seed varietal not disclosed in sources reviewed)
plan.background: A collaboration between Altadis USA and the Tommy Bahama lifestyle brand, conceived by Rafael Nodal and A.J. Fernandez. Announced for a late-summer/September 2025 launch. Marketed as an 'elegant, relaxed, island-inspired' lifestyle collaboration; medium body.

plan.name: Abuelo
plan.background: 100% Honduran puro made entirely from tobacco grown on the Eiroa/JRE Tobacco Farm in Las Lomas, Jamastran, Honduras, and produced at Fabrica de Puros Aladino S.A. (Julio R. Eiroa's factory). Released June 2021. Vitola names form a family-relationship theme (Abuelo = grandfather, Padre = father, Nieto/Nieta = grandson/granddaughter).

plan.name: Alfonso Extra Añejo
plan.background: Marketed on unitedcigargroup.com simply as 'Alfonso Añejo'. Aged 5+ years, finished in French oak-lined rooms. Produced by Selected Tobacco S.A. (also makers of Atabey and Byron), named after Nelson Alfonso Egüed.

plan.name: Alfonso Gran Selección
plan.filler: Dominican & Nicaraguan (one source: Dominican & Peruvian - minor cross-source discrepancy)
plan.background: Companion/darker blend to the Extra Añejo, using extended cedar + French oak aging. Produced at Tabacos de Costa Rica.

plan.name: Bandolero
plan.story_short: Bandolero was created by Nelson Alfonso, founder of Selected Tobacco S.A., and is distributed in the U.S. by United Cigars. Rolled at Tabacos de Costa Rica, it is organized into three core series distinguished by wrapper shade, plus a newer premium line aged in Madrid, Spain.

plan.name: Bandolero Serie A (Aventureros)
plan.background: Created by Nelson Alfonso (founder of Selected Tobacco S.A.); distributed in the U.S. by United Cigars (David Garofalo's company). Blends are largely undisclosed/proprietary. Organized into three core series distinguished by wrapper shade, plus a newer premium line.

plan.name: Bandolero Serie C (Clandestinos)
plan.wrapper: Ecuadorian Connecticut (lightest of the three series)
plan.background: Created by Nelson Alfonso (founder of Selected Tobacco S.A.); distributed in the U.S. by United Cigars (David Garofalo's company). Blends are largely undisclosed/proprietary. Organized into three core series distinguished by wrapper shade, plus a newer premium line.

plan.name: Bandolero Serie T (Traficantes)
plan.wrapper: Natural/Colorado-shade (medium hue, between Serie A and C)
plan.filler: Undisclosed; Peruvian ligero noted for Tremendos
plan.background: Created by Nelson Alfonso (founder of Selected Tobacco S.A.); distributed in the U.S. by United Cigars (David Garofalo's company). Blends are largely undisclosed/proprietary. Organized into three core series distinguished by wrapper shade, plus a newer premium line.

plan.name: Bandolero Premium
plan.background: Launched ~2025; rolled at Tabacos de Costa Rica, then aged 3 years in Madrid, Spain in cedar-lined humidors.

plan.name: Firecracker
plan.story_short: Firecracker dates to 2007, when it was exclusive to Two Guys Smoke Shop in New Hampshire; United Cigars now distributes it nationwide. Its signature format is a 3.5 x 50 petite robusto with a pigtail cap resembling a fuse.

plan.name: Firecracker (Connecticut)
plan.background: Line dating to 2007, originally exclusive to Two Guys Smoke Shop in NH; now distributed nationwide by United Cigars. Multiple SKUs exist (Connecticut, Maduro, Sungrown, and a 2024/2026 'Independence Firecracker' 250th-anniversary edition).

plan.name: Independence Firecracker
plan.background: Made at Arnold André Dominicana; sold in 12-count tins, $9 MSRP. Part of United's Independence 250th-anniversary series (halfwheel, 2026). Maduro and Sungrown SKUs also exist under the Firecracker name.

plan.name: Garofalo
plan.story_short: Garofalo La Famiglia was released by United Cigars, owned by David Garofalo, and named for his family. It is made by Tabacalera Perdomo in Nicaragua, was announced in December 2021 and shipped to retailers in January 2022.

plan.name: La Famiglia
plan.wrapper: CT: Ecuadorian Connecticut / MD: Nicaraguan Maduro (bourbon-barrel-aged) / SG: Nicaraguan Sun Grown
plan.background: 'Garofalo La Famiglia' is a cigar line released by United Cigars (New Hampshire, owned by David Garofalo), named after Garofalo's own family. Manufactured by Tabacalera Perdomo (Nick Perdomo) in Nicaragua. Announced Dec 2021, shipped to retailers January 2022.

plan.name: Gold Star
plan.story_short: Gold Star was first introduced in 1995 and lay dormant for years before a 2024 limited-edition revival supporting the Navy SEAL Gold Star Program. It moved into full regular production in March 2025, with a wider rollout after the April 2025 PCA trade show.

plan.name: Gold Star (regular production, 2025)
plan.filler: Dominican (Ligero, Criollo '98, Corojo '98) blended with Connecticut Broadleaf
plan.background: Boxes of 20. Differs from the 2024 LE version primarily in binder (Sumatra vs. Ecuadoran) and a higher ligero/broadleaf ratio.

plan.name: Hightower
plan.story_short: Hightower is marketed as JD Hightower by Jose Dominguez and made at the Magia Cubana factory in the Dominican Republic. Reviews date back to at least 2012, before United Cigars became involved.

plan.name: Hightower (Maduro) by Jose Dominguez
plan.background: Marketed as 'JD Hightower by Jose Dominguez', made at Magia Cubana factory, Dominican Republic. Reviews date back to at least 2012, predating United Cigars' involvement.

plan.name: La Gianna Havana
plan.factory: Diadema Cigars de Honduras S.A., Danlí, Honduras
plan.story_short: La Gianna Havana is a United Cigars brand first released in 1994 and named to commemorate the birth of David Garofalo's daughter. It is handcrafted at Diadema Cigars de Honduras in Danlí, Honduras.

plan.name: La Gianna Havana Natural
plan.background: United Cigars brand (David Garofalo), originally released in 1994, named to commemorate the birth of Garofalo's daughter. Handcrafted at Diadema Cigars de Honduras S.A. in Danlí, Honduras.

plan.name: La Gianna Havana Maduro
plan.background: United Cigars brand (David Garofalo), originally released in 1994, named to commemorate the birth of Garofalo's daughter. Handcrafted at Diadema Cigars de Honduras S.A. in Danlí, Honduras.

plan.name: La Gianna Havana Angelic
plan.background: Distinct sweet-tip blend, separate SKU from Natural/Maduro.

plan.name: La Gianna Havana 30th Anniversary
plan.wrapper: Barber pole: Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed + Mexican San Andrés
plan.filler: Dominican Republic, Honduras, and U.S. tobaccos
plan.background: Celebrates the brand's 1994 origin; PCA 2024 release.

plan.name: Montosa
plan.story_short: Montosa is produced by Arnold André in the Dominican Republic from Cibao Valley tobaccos and distributed in the U.S. by United Cigars. The Montosa Maduro was named Cigar of the Year 2022 by The Cigar Authority.

plan.name: Montosa Natural
plan.background: Produced by Arnold André (Dominican factory, est. Tobaccos sourced from the Cibao Valley, Dominican Republic. Montosa Maduro named 'Cigar of the Year 2022' by The Cigar Authority.

plan.name: Montosa Maduro
plan.background: Produced by Arnold André (Dominican factory, est. Tobaccos sourced from the Cibao Valley, Dominican Republic. Montosa Maduro named 'Cigar of the Year 2022' by The Cigar Authority.

plan.name: Red Anchor
plan.story_short: Red Anchor is a naval-rank-themed line distributed by United Cigars and made at the Kelner Boutique Factory. The Admiral was released in 2022, followed by the Captain, Commodore, Gunner and Cooper, announced at PCA 2023.

plan.name: Red Anchor
plan.filler: Dominican San Vicente, Dominican Habano '92, Pennsylvania tobacco
plan.background: Single blend across all vitolas, differing only in shape/size.

plan.name: Terra Nova
plan.story_short: Terra Nova is manufactured by Arnold André Dominicana in the Dominican Republic and has been distributed in the U.S. by United Cigars and Two Guys Cigars under a January 2022 deal.

plan.name: Araperique
plan.filler: Includes Araperique tobacco (a rare varietal, barrel-aged in oak whiskey casks) plus other Dominican filler tobaccos
plan.background: Flavor notes: pepper, floral, hay, cedar, cinnamon, peanuts, fruit zest, butter, fig, dark chocolate, oak.

plan.name: Dark Fired Kentucky
plan.filler: Dominican, Nicaraguan, Brazilian tobaccos plus Dark Fired Kentucky leaf
plan.background: 20-count boxes. Cigar Coop rated the Toro 88 pts.

plan.name: United
plan.wrapper: Natural/Connecticut: Ecuadorian Habano (marketed as 'Sun Grown'); Maduro: Mexican San Andrés
plan.filler: Dominican Broadleaf, Quisqueya, Dominican Seco, Dominican Olor
plan.background: Produced at Tabacalera Magia, Dominican Republic. Currently sold in a box-pressed-to-'Round' production format.

plan.name: YaYa
plan.story_short: YaYa was created by Carlos Guillermo and launched in the Dominican Republic in 2019, with its U.S. debut through United Cigars at the PCA 2022 trade show. The name nods to a woman nicknamed Yaya who rolled her own blends.

plan.name: YaYa
plan.background: Created by Carlos Guillermo, originally launched in the Dominican Republic in 2019; United Cigars gave it its U.S. debut at the PCA 2022 trade show. Name references a woman nicknamed 'Yaya' who rolled her own blends, from whom Guillermo and friends used to take cigars as kids.

plan.name: VegaFina
plan.story_short: VegaFina is named for its 1998 founding year and has historically been far stronger in Europe than in the U.S. The brand is owned by Tabacalera USA and distributed in the U.S. by Altadis USA; its production has been disrupted since 2025 by sanctions affecting its main factory.

plan.name: VegaFina 1998
plan.background: A step up in complexity from the core line.

plan.name: VegaFina Original
plan.background: The core/original line. Positioned as an affordable, widely-popular cigar in Europe; smooth, aromatic, medium-bodied.
